summary_en: Consul Fabius Gurges fought unsuccessfully against the Samnites, and when the senate considered removing him his father Fabius Maximus averted the disgrace by promising to serve as his son's legate.
quote_la: Cum Fabius Gurges cos. male adversus Samnites pugnasset et senatus de removendo eo ab exercitu ageret

summary_en: Aided by his father's counsel, the consul slaughtered the Samnites and triumphed, executing the Samnite commander C. Pontius after leading him in the triumph.
quote_la: C. Pontium, imperatorem Samnitium, ductum in triumpho, securi percussit.

summary_en: During a pestilence envoys brought the serpent embodying Aesculapius from Epidaurus, and a temple to Aesculapius was established where it went ashore on the Tiber island.
quote_la: missi legati ut Aesculapi signum Romam ab Epidauro transferrent

summary_en: The ex-consul L. Postumius was condemned because, while commanding an army, he had used his soldiers' labor on his own land.
quote_la: L. Postumius consularis, quoniam, cum exercitui praeesset, opera militum in agro suo usus erat, damnatus est.

summary_en: At the Samnites' request for peace, the treaty with them was renewed for the fourth time.
quote_la: Pacem petentibus Samnitibus foedus quarto renovatum est.

summary_en: Consul Curius Dentatus slaughtered the Samnites, defeated the rebellious Sabines and accepted their surrender, and triumphed twice in the same magistracy.
quote_la: Curius Dentatus cos. Samnitibus caesis et Sabinis, qui rebellaverant, victis et in deditionem acceptis bis in eodem magistratu triumphavit.

summary_en: Colonies were founded at Castrum, Sena, and Hadria.
quote_la: Coloniae deductae sunt Castrum Sena Hadria.

summary_en: The triumviri capitales were then created for the first time.
quote_la: Triumviri capitales tunc primum creati sunt.

summary_en: A census was held and the lustrum closed; the citizen heads counted were CCLXXII (272,000).
quote_la: Censu acto lustrum conditum est. Censa sunt civium capita | CCLXXII |.

summary_en: The plebs, because of debt and after grave and long seditions, finally seceded to the Janiculum, whence the dictator Q. Hortensius led them back, dying in that very magistracy.
quote_la: Plebs propter aes alienum post graves et longas seditiones ad ultimum secessit in Ianiculum

summary_en: The book also contained campaigns against the Vulsinienses and against the Lucanians, against whom it had been decided to bring aid to the Thurians.
quote_la: Res praeterea contra Vulsinienses gestas continet, item adversus Lucanos

summary_en: After Roman envoys were killed by the Senonian Gauls, war was declared on the Gauls, and the praetor L. Caecilius was cut down with his legions by them.
quote_la: Cum legati Romanorum a Gallis Senonibus interfecti essent, bello ob id Gallis indicto

summary_en: The Tarentines plundered a Roman fleet and killed its commanding duumvir, then assaulted the senate's envoys sent to complain, and war was declared on them.
quote_la: Cum a Tarentinis classis Romana direpta esset, IIuiro, qui praeerat classi, occiso

summary_en: The Samnites revolted, and successful battles were fought against them, the Lucanians, the Bruttii, and the Etruscans by several commanders.
quote_la: Aduersus eos et Lucanos et Brittios et Etruscos aliquot proeliis a compluribus ducibus bene pugnatum est.

summary_en: Pyrrhus, king of the Epirotes, came to Italy to bring aid to the Tarentines.
quote_la: Pyrrhus, Epirotarum rex, ut auxilium Tarentinis ferret, in Italiam uenit.

summary_en: A Campanian legion sent with prefect Decius Vibullius to garrison Regium killed the inhabitants and seized the town.
quote_la: Cum in praesidium Reginorum legio Campana cum praefecto Decio Vibullio missa esset, occisis Reginis Regium occupauit.

summary_en: Consul Valerius Laevinus fought with little success against Pyrrhus, the soldiers terrified chiefly by the unfamiliar appearance of the elephants.
quote_la: Valerius Laeuinus cos. parum prospere aduersus Pyrrhum pugnauit, elephantorum maxime inusitata facie territis militibus.

summary_en: Inspecting the bodies of the Romans fallen in battle, Pyrrhus found all their wounds facing the enemy, and he advanced plundering toward the city of Rome.
quote_la: omnia uersa in hostem inuenit populabundusque ad urbem Romanam processit.

summary_en: C. Fabricius, sent by the senate to negotiate the ransom of captives, was tempted in vain by the king to desert his country, and the captives were returned without ransom.
quote_la: C. Fabricius missus ad eum a senatu, ut de redimendis captiuis ageret, frustra ut patriam desereret a rege temptatus est.

summary_en: Cineas, sent by Pyrrhus as envoy to the senate to ask that the king be admitted to the city to arrange peace, was refused after Appius Claudius came to the senate-house and carried his opinion.
quote_la: Cineas legatus a Pyrrho ad senatum missus petiit ut conponendae pacis causa rex in urbem reciperetur.

summary_en: The censor Cn. Domitius, the first from the plebs to close the lustrum, held the census: 287,222 citizen heads were counted.
quote_la: Cn. Domitius censor primus ex plebe lustrum condidit. Censa sunt ciuium capita CCLXXXVII milia CCXXII.

summary_en: A second battle was fought against Pyrrhus with indecisive outcome.
quote_la: Iterum aduersus Pyrrhum dubio euentu pugnatum est.

summary_en: The treaty with the Carthaginians was renewed for the fourth time.
quote_la: Cum Carthaginiensibus quarto foedus renouatum est.

summary_en: When a deserter from Pyrrhus promised consul C. Fabricius that he would give the king poison, he was sent back to the king with information of the offer.
quote_la: Cum C. Fabricio consuli is qui ad eum a Pyrrho transfugerat, polliceretur uenenum se regi daturum

summary_en: The book also contained successful campaigns against the Lucanians, Bruttii, Samnites, and Etruscans.
quote_la: Res praeterea contra Lucanos et Bruttios, Samnites et Etruscos prospere gestas continet.

summary_en: Pyrrhus crossed over to Sicily.
quote_la: Pyrrhus in Siciliam traiecit. Cum inter alia prodigia

summary_en: Among other prodigies, the statue of Jupiter on the Capitol was thrown down by lightning, and its head was found by the haruspices.
quote_la: Cum inter alia prodigia fulmine deiectum esset in Capitolio Iouis signum, caput eius per haruspices inuentum est.

summary_en: Consul Curius Dentatus, holding a levy, was the first to sell the goods of a man who did not respond when summoned.
quote_la: eius, qui citatus non responderat, bona primus uendidit

summary_en: Curius Dentatus defeated Pyrrhus, who had returned from Sicily to Italy, and drove him out of Italy.
quote_la: iterum Pyrrhum ex Sicilia in Italiam reuersum uicit et Italia expulit.

summary_en: The censor Fabricius removed the ex-consul P. Cornelius Rufinus from the senate because he possessed ten pounds of wrought silver.
quote_la: Fabricius censor P. Cornelium Rufinum consularem senatu mouit, quod is X pondo argenti facti haberet.

summary_en: The lustrum was closed by the censors: 271,224 citizen heads were counted.
quote_la: Lustro a censoribus condito censa sunt ciuium capita CCLXXI milia CCXXIIII.

summary_en: An alliance was made with Ptolemy, king of Egypt.
quote_la: Cum Ptolemaeo, Aegypti rege, societas iuncta est.

summary_en: Sextilia, a Vestal virgin, was condemned for unchastity and buried alive.
quote_la: Sextilia, uirgo Vestalis, damnata incesti uiua defossa est.

summary_en: Colonies were founded at Posidonia and Cosa.
quote_la: Coloniae deductae sunt Posidonia et Cosa.

summary_en: A Carthaginian fleet came to the aid of the Tarentines, by which act the treaty was violated by them.
quote_la: Carthaginiensium classis auxilio Tarentinis uenit, quo facto ab his foedus uiolatum est.

summary_en: The book also contained successful campaigns against the Lucanians, Bruttii, and Samnites, and the death of king Pyrrhus.
quote_la: Res praeterea contra Lucanos et Bruttios et Samnites feliciter gestas et Pyrrhi regis mortem continet.

summary_en: The Tarentines were defeated and given peace and freedom.
quote_la: Victis Tarentinis pax et libertas data est.

summary_en: The Campanian legion which had seized Regium was besieged, surrendered, and was beheaded.
quote_la: Legio Campana, quae Regium occupauerat, obsessa deditione facta securi percussa est.

summary_en: Young men who had assaulted envoys of the Apolloniates sent to the senate were handed over to the Apolloniates.
quote_la: Cum legatos Apolloniatium ad senatum missos quidam iuuenes pulsassent, dediti sunt Apolloniatibus.

summary_en: The Picentes were defeated and given peace.
quote_la: Picentibus uictis pax data est. Coloniae

summary_en: Colonies were founded at Ariminum in Picenum and Beneventum in Samnium.
quote_la: Coloniae deductae Ariminum in Piceno, Beneuentum in Samnio.

summary_en: Then for the first time the Roman people began to use silver money.
quote_la: Tunc primum populus R. argento uti coepit.

summary_en: The Umbrians and Sallentines were defeated and received in surrender.
quote_la: Vmbri et Sallentini uicti in deditionem accepti sunt.

summary_en: The number of quaestors was increased so that there were eight.
quote_la: Quaestorum numerus ampliatus est, ut essent VIII.

summary_en: The origin of the Carthaginians and the beginnings of their city are related.
quote_la: Origo Carthaginiensium et primordia urbis eorum referuntur.

summary_en: After a contested debate, the senate decreed that aid be brought to the Mamertines against the Carthaginians and Hiero, king of the Syracusans.
quote_la: Contra quos et Hieronem, regem Syracusanorum, auxilium Mamertinis ferendum senatus censuit

summary_en: Roman armies then crossed the sea for the first time, fought repeatedly with success against Hiero, and granted him peace at his request.
quote_la: transgressisque tunc primum mare exercitibus Romanis aduersus Hieronem saepius bene pugnatum. Petenti pax data est.

summary_en: The lustrum was closed by the censors: 382,234 citizen heads were counted.
quote_la: Lustrum a censoribus conditum est. Censa sunt ciuium capita CCCLXXXII milia CCXXXIIII.

summary_en: Decimus Junius Brutus was the first to give a gladiatorial show, in honor of his deceased father.
quote_la: Decimus Iunius Brutus munus gladiatorium in honorem defuncti patris primus edidit.

summary_en: A colony was founded at Aesernia.
quote_la: Colonia Aesernia deducta est. Res praeterea

summary_en: The book also contained successful campaigns against the Carthaginians and the Vulsinii.
quote_la: Res praeterea contra Poenos et Vulsinios prospere gestas continet.

summary_en: Consul Cn. Cornelius was surrounded by the Punic fleet and captured by treachery, lured out as if to a parley.
quote_la: Cn. Cornelius consul a classe Punica circumuentus et per fraudem, ueluti in conloquium euocatus, captus est.

summary_en: Consul C. Duillius fought successfully against the Carthaginian fleet and, first of all Roman commanders, celebrated a triumph for a naval victory, receiving the perpetual honor of a torch and flute-player when returning from dinner.
quote_la: C. Duillius consul aduersus classem Poenorum prospere pugnauit, primusque omnium Romanorum ducum naualis uictoriae duxit triumphum.

summary_en: Consul L. Cornelius fought successfully in Sardinia and Corsica against the Sardinians, Corsicans, and the Carthaginian commander Hanno.
quote_la: L. Cornelius consul in Sardinia et Corsica contra Sardos et Corsos et Hannonem, Poenorum ducem, feliciter pugnauit.

summary_en: Consul Atilius Calatinus, having rashly led his army into a place surrounded by the Carthaginians, escaped through the valor of the military tribune M. Calpurnius, who with 300 soldiers made a sortie and drew the enemy upon himself.
quote_la: M. Calpurni, tribuni militum, uirtute et opera euasit, qui cum CCC militibus eruptione facta hostes in se conuerterat.

summary_en: Hannibal, the Carthaginian commander, after the fleet he commanded was defeated, was crucified by his own soldiers.
quote_la: Hannibal, dux Poenorum, uicta classe cui praefuerat, a militibus suis in crucem sublatus est.

summary_en: Consul Atilius Regulus, after defeating the Carthaginians in a naval battle, crossed over to Africa.
quote_la: Atilius Regulus cos. uictis nauali proelio Poenis in Africam traiecit.

summary_en: Atilius Regulus in Africa killed a serpent of portentous size with great loss of his soldiers.
quote_la: Atilius Regulus in Africa serpentem portentosae magnitudinis cum magna clade militum occidit

summary_en: After fighting several successful battles against the Carthaginians, Regulus complained by letter to the senate that no successor was sent him, among his reasons that his little farm had been abandoned by its hired laborers.
quote_la: successorque ei a senatu prospere bellum gerenti non mitteretur, id ipsum per litteras ad senatum scriptas questus est

summary_en: Regulus was defeated in battle and captured by Xanthippus, the Lacedaemonian commander summoned by the Carthaginians.
quote_la: arcessito a Carthaginiensibus Xanthippo, Lacedaemoniorum duce, uictus proelio et captus est.

summary_en: Operations otherwise conducted successfully by all the Roman commanders on land and sea were marred by shipwrecks of the fleets.
quote_la: Res deinde a ducibus Romanis omnibus terra marique prospere gestas deformauerunt naufragia classium.

summary_en: Tib. Coruncanius was the first man from the plebs created pontifex maximus.
quote_la: Tib. Coruncanius primus ex plebe pontifex maximus creatus est.

summary_en: The censors M'. Valerius Maximus and P. Sempronius Sophus, in revising the senate roll, removed sixteen men from the senate.
quote_la: M'. Valerius Maximus P. Sempronius Sophus censores cum senatum legerent, XVI senatu mouerunt.

summary_en: The censors closed the lustrum, in which 297,797 citizen heads were counted.
quote_la: Lustrum condiderunt, quo censa sunt ciuium capita CCXCVII milia DCCXCVII.

summary_en: Regulus, sent by the Carthaginians to the senate to treat for peace or an exchange of captives and bound by oath to return, advised the senate against both, kept his faith by returning, and perished under Carthaginian torture.
quote_la: cum fide custodita reuersus esset, supplicio a Carthaginiensibus de eo sumpto periit.

summary_en: Caecilius Metellus, after successful operations against the Carthaginians, celebrated a splendid triumph in which 13 enemy leaders and 120 elephants were led.
quote_la: Caecilius Metellus rebus aduersus Poenos prospere gestis speciosum egit triumphum, XIII ducibus hostium et CXX elephantis in eo ductis.

summary_en: Consul Claudius Pulcher, setting out against the auspices and ordering the chickens that would not feed to be drowned, fought unsuccessfully at sea against the Carthaginians.
quote_la: Claudius Pulcher cos. contra auspicia profectus - iussit mergi pullos, qui cibari nolebant - infeliciter aduersus Carthaginienses classe pugnauit

summary_en: Recalled by the senate and ordered to name a dictator, Claudius Pulcher named Claudius Glicia, a man of the lowest rank, who, though forced to abdicate, afterwards watched the games in his magistrate's toga.
quote_la: iussusque dictatorem dicere Claudium Gliciam dixit, sortis ultimae hominem

summary_en: A. Atilius Calatinus was the first dictator to lead an army outside Italy.
quote_la: A. Atilius Calatinus primus dictator extra Italiam exercitum duxit.

summary_en: An exchange of captives was made with the Carthaginians.
quote_la: Commutatio captiuorum cum Poenis facta est.

summary_en: Colonies were founded at Fregenae and at Brundisium in the Sallentine territory.
quote_la: Coloniae deductae sunt Fregenae, in agro Sallentino Brundisium.

summary_en: The lustrum was closed by the censors: 241,212 citizen heads were counted.
quote_la: Lustrum a censoribus conditum est. Censa sunt ciuium capita CCXLI milia CCXII.

summary_en: Claudia, sister of P. Claudius, pressed by the crowd when returning from the games, wished her brother alive to lose another fleet, and a fine was imposed on her for this remark.
quote_la: Claudia, soror P. Claudi qui contemptis auspiciis male pugnauerat, a ludis reuertens cum turba premeretur

summary_en: Two praetors were then created for the first time.
quote_la: Duo praetores tunc primum creati sunt.

summary_en: Caecilius Metellus, pontifex maximus, kept the consul A. Postumius, who was also flamen Martialis, in the city when he wished to set out for war, not allowing him to leave the sacred rites.
quote_la: cum is ad bellum gerendum proficisci uellet, in urbe tenuit nec passus est a sacris recedere.

summary_en: After successful operations by several commanders against the Carthaginians, consul C. Lutatius completed the victory by defeating the Punic fleet at the Aegates islands.
quote_la: summam uictoriae C. Lutatius cos. uicta ad Aegates insulas classe Poenorum imposuit.

summary_en: Peace was granted to the Carthaginians at their request.
quote_la: Petentibus Carthaginiensibus pax data est.

summary_en: When the temple of Vesta burned, the pontifex maximus Caecilius Metellus snatched the sacred objects from the fire.
quote_la: Cum templum Vestae arderet, Caecilius Metellus, pontifex maximus, ex incendio sacra rapuit.

summary_en: Two tribes were added, the Velina and the Quirina.
quote_la: Duae tribus adiectae sunt, Velina et Quirina.

summary_en: The Falisci rebelled and were thoroughly subdued and surrendered on the sixth day.
quote_la: Falisci cum rebellassent, sexto die perdomiti in deditionem uenerunt.

summary_en: A colony was founded at Spoletium.
quote_la: Spoletium colonia deducta est. Aduersus

summary_en: An army was then advanced for the first time against the Ligurians.
quote_la: Aduersus Liguras tunc primum exercitus promotus est.

summary_en: The Sardinians and Corsicans rebelled and were subdued.
quote_la: Sardi et Corsi cum rebellassent, subacti sunt.

summary_en: Tuccia, a Vestal virgin, was condemned for unchastity.
quote_la: Tuccia, uirgo Vestalis, incesti damnata est.

summary_en: War was declared on the Illyrians because one of the envoys sent to them had been killed, and they were subdued and surrendered.
quote_la: Bellum Illyriis propter unum ex legatis, qui ad eos missi erant, occisum indictum est

summary_en: The number of praetors was increased so that there were four.
quote_la: Praetorum numerus ampliatus est ut essent IIII.

summary_en: The Transalpine Gauls who had broken into Italy were cut down.
quote_la: Galli transalpini, qui in Italiam inruperant, caesi sunt.

summary_en: In that war, Livy says, the Roman people had 800,000 armed men of their own and of the Latin name.
quote_la: Eo bello populum R. sui Latinique nominis DCCC milia armatorum habuisse dicit.

summary_en: Roman armies were then led across the Po for the first time, and the Insubrian Gauls were routed in several battles and surrendered.
quote_la: Exercitibus Romanis tunc primum trans Padum ductis Galli Insubres aliquot proeliis fusi in deditionem uenerunt.

summary_en: Consul M. Claudius Marcellus killed Vertomarus, leader of the Insubrian Gauls, and brought back the spolia opima.
quote_la: M. Claudius Marcellus cos. occiso Gallorum Insubrium duce, Vertomaro, opima spolia rettulit.

summary_en: The Istrians were subdued, and the Illyrians, who had rebelled again, were tamed and surrendered.
quote_la: Histri subacti sunt. Iterum Illyrii cum rebellassent, domiti in deditionem uenerunt.

summary_en: The lustrum was closed by the censors three times; at the first lustrum 270,212 citizen heads were counted.
quote_la: Lustrum a censoribus ter conditum est. Primo lustro censa sunt ciuium capita CCLXX milia CCXII.

summary_en: The freedmen, previously dispersed through all the tribes, were confined to four: the Esquiline, Palatine, Suburan, and Colline.
quote_la: Libertini in quattuor tribus redacti sunt, cum antea dispersi per omnes fuissent

summary_en: The censor C. Flaminius built the Via Flaminia and constructed the Circus Flaminius.
quote_la: C. Flaminius censor uiam Flaminiam muniit et circum Flaminium exstruxit.

summary_en: Colonies were founded at Placentia and Cremona in territory captured from the Gauls.
quote_la: Coloniae deductae sunt in agro de Gallis capto Placentia et Cremona.

summary_en: When king Eumenes, who had been neutral in the Macedonian war, came to Rome, a general law was passed that no king be permitted to come to Rome.
quote_la: in commune lex lata est, ne cui regi Romam venire liceret.

summary_en: Consul Claudius Marcellus subdued the Alpine Gauls and consul C. Sulpicius Gallus the Ligurians.
quote_la: Claudius Marcellus consul Alpinos Gallos, C. Sulpicius Gallus consul Liguras subegit.

summary_en: Envoys of king Prusias complained about Eumenes, that he was ravaging their territory, and said he had conspired with Antiochus against the Roman people.
quote_la: legati Prusiae regis questi sunt de Eumene, quod fines suos popularetur

summary_en: An alliance was made with the Rhodians at their entreaty.
quote_la: societas cum Rhodiis deprecantibus iuncta est.

summary_en: The lustrum was closed by the censors: citizen heads counted were CCCXXXVII XXII (337,022).
quote_la: lustrum a censoribus conditum: censa sunt civium capita CCCXXXVII XXII.

summary_en: M. Aemilius Lepidus was made princeps senatus.
quote_la: princeps senatus M. Aemilius Lepidus.

summary_en: Ptolemy, king of Egypt, driven from his kingdom by his younger brother, was restored by envoys sent to him.
quote_la: Ptolemaeus Aegypti rex, pulsus regno a minore fratre missis ad cum legatis restitutus est.

summary_en: On the death of Ariarathes, king of Cappadocia, his son Ariarathes received the kingdom and renewed friendship with the Roman people through envoys.
quote_la: filius eius Ariarathes regnum accepit et amicitiam cum populo Romano per legatos renovavit.

summary_en: The book also contained operations with varying outcome against the Ligurians, Corsicans, and Lusitanians.
quote_la: res praeterea adversus Liguras et Corsos et Lusitanos vario eventu gestas

summary_en: Amid disturbances in Syria after the death of Antiochus, Demetrius son of Seleucus, a hostage at Rome, slipped away secretly, killed the boy Antiochus with his guardian Lysias, and was received into the kingdom.
quote_la: hunc Antiochum puerum cum Lysia tutore Demetrius Seleuci filius, qui Romae obses fuerat

summary_en: L. Aemilius Paulus, conqueror of Perseus, died; his integrity was so great that the auction of his goods scarcely paid his wife's dowry despite the immense wealth he had brought from Spain and Macedonia.
quote_la: L. Aemilius Paulus, qui Persen vicerat, mortuus.

summary_en: The Pomptine marshes were drained by consul Cornelius Cethegus, to whom that province had fallen, and made into farmland.
quote_la: Pomptinae paludes a Cornelio Cethego consule, cui ea provincia evenerat, siccatae

summary_en: A fine was imposed on the praetor Cn. Tremellius because he had wrongfully contended with the pontifex maximus M. Aemilius Lepidus; the claim of religion proved stronger than that of magistrates.
quote_la: Cn. Tremellio pr. multa dicta est, quod cum M. Aemilio Lepido pontifice maximo iniuriose contenderat

summary_en: A law on electoral bribery (de ambitu) was passed.
quote_la: lex de ambitu lata. lustrum a censoribus

summary_en: The lustrum was closed by the censors: citizen heads counted were CCCXXVIII CCCXVI (328,316).
quote_la: lustrum a censoribus conditum est: censa sunt civium capita CCCXXVIII CCCXVI.

summary_en: Aemilius Lepidus was made princeps senatus for the sixth time.
quote_la: princeps senatus sextum Aemilius Lepidus.

summary_en: A pact was struck between the quarreling Ptolemy brothers, that one should rule in Egypt, the other at Cyrene.
quote_la: inter Ptolemaeos fratres, qui dissidebant, foedus ictum, ut alter Aegypto, alter Cyrenis regnaret.

summary_en: Ariarathes, king of Cappadocia, driven from his kingdom by the scheme and forces of Demetrius, king of Syria, was restored by the senate.
quote_la: Ariarathes, Cappadociae rex, consilio Demetrii Syriae regis et viribus pulsus regno, a senatu restitutus est.

summary_en: Men were sent by the senate to judge between Masinissa and the Carthaginians concerning land.
quote_la: missi a senatu, qui inter Masinissam et Carthaginienses de agro iudicarent.

summary_en: Consul C. Marcius fought against the Dalmatians, at first with little success, afterwards successfully; the same people was subdued by consul Cornelius Nasica.
quote_la: C. Marcius consul adversus Dalmatas primum parum prospere, postea, feliciter pugnavit.

summary_en: Consul Q. Opimius subdued the Transalpine Ligurians, who were ravaging Antipolis and Nicaea, towns of the Massiliotes.
quote_la: Q. Opimius consul Transalpinos Liguras, qui Massiliensium oppida Antipolim et Nicaeam vastabant, subegit.

summary_en: The book also contained operations in Spain conducted with little success by several commanders.
quote_la: praeterea res in Hispania a compluribus parum prospere gestas continet.

summary_en: In the 598th year from the founding of the city the consuls began to enter office on the Kalends of January, the elections being changed because the Spaniards were in rebellion.
quote_la: consules anno quingentesimo nonagesimo octavo ab urbe condita magistratum kal. Ian. inire coeperunt.

summary_en: Envoys sent to arbitrate between the Carthaginians and Masinissa reported that they had discovered a quantity of naval timber at Carthage.
quote_la: legati ad disceptandum inter Carthaginienses et Masinissam missi nuntiaverunt vim navalis materiae se Carthagine deprehendisse.

summary_en: Several praetors were accused on charges of avarice in their provinces and condemned.
quote_la: aliquot praetores a provinciis avaritiae nomine accusati damnati sunt.

summary_en: The lustrum was closed by the censors: citizen heads counted were CCCXXIIII.
quote_la: lustrum a censoribus conditum est: censa sunt civium capita CCCXXIIII.

summary_en: The seeds of the Third Punic War are related.
quote_la: semina tertii Punici belli referuntur.

summary_en: When a great Numidian army under Ariobarzanes was reported in Carthaginian territory, M. Porcius Cato urged declaring war on Carthage, but on P. Cornelius Nasica's opposing view it was decided to send envoys to Carthage to observe.
quote_la: contra dicente P. Cornelio Nasica placuit legatos mitti Carthaginem, qui specularentur, quid ageretur.

summary_en: The envoys, attempting to make peace between Carthage and Masinissa, were endangered when the magistrate Gisgo son of Hamilcar stirred the people to war against Rome, and escaped violence only by flight.
quote_la: ita populum concitavit bellum adversus Romanos suadendo, ut legatos, quo minus violarentur, fuga explicuerit.

summary_en: M. Porcius Cato, being poor, gave his son, who died during his praetorship, a funeral at the slightest possible expense.
quote_la: M. Porcius Cato filii in praetura mortui funus tenuissimo

summary_en: Andriscus, who with enormous insistence falsely claimed to be the son of Perseus, once king of Macedonia, was sent to Rome.
quote_la: Andriscus, qui se Persei filium, regis quondam Macedoniae, ingenti adserveratione mentiretur, Romam missus.

summary_en: M. Aemilius Lepidus, chosen princeps senatus by six successive pairs of censors, before dying instructed his sons to carry out his funeral modestly, since the funerals of great men were ennobled by ancestral images, not expense.
quote_la: M. Aemilius Lepidus, qui princeps senatus sextis iam censoribus lectus erat

summary_en: An inquiry into poisonings was held: the noblewomen Publilia and Licinia, accused of killing their consular husbands, were put to death by decree of their kinsmen after the case was heard.
quote_la: Publilia et Licinia, nobiles feminae, quae viros suos consulares necasse insimulabantur

summary_en: Gulussa, son of Masinissa, reported that levies were being held at Carthage, a fleet being prepared, and war undoubtedly being contrived; it was decided to send ten envoys to investigate.
quote_la: Gulussa Masinissae filius nuntiavit Carthagine dilectus agi, classem comparari et haud dubie bellum strui.

summary_en: The consuls L. Licinius Lucullus and A. Postumius Albinus, conducting the levy strictly and exempting no one by favor, were thrown into prison by the tribunes of the plebs.
quote_la: ab tribunis plebis, qui pro amicis suis vacationem impetrare non poterant, in carcerem coniecti sunt.

summary_en: When the unsuccessful Spanish war so dismayed the citizens that none would serve as tribunes or legates, P. Cornelius Aemilianus stepped forward and professed he would accept any military service, rousing everyone to enthusiasm for service.
quote_la: P. Cornelius Aemilianus processit et exceptaturum se militiae genus, quodcumque imperatum esset, professus est

summary_en: Consul Lucullus subdued the Vaccaei, the Cantabri, and other peoples hitherto unknown in Spain.
quote_la: Vaccaeos et Cantabros et alias incognitas adhuc in Hispania gentes subegit.

summary_en: There P. Cornelius Scipio Aemilianus, as military tribune, killed a barbarian challenger and ran still greater danger at the storming of the city of Intercatia, being the first to scale the wall.
quote_la: provocatorem barbarum tribunus militum occidit et in expugnatione Intercatiae urbis maius etiamnum periculum adit

summary_en: The praetor Ser. Sulpicius Galba fought badly against the Lusitanians.
quote_la: Ser. Sulpicius Galba praetor male adversus Lusitanos pugnavit.

summary_en: When envoys returned from Africa reporting an army and fleet at Carthage, the senate resolved to abstain from war if the Carthaginians burned their fleet and dismissed their army; otherwise the next consuls should bring up the question of a Punic war.
quote_la: placuit, ut bello abstinerent, si Carthaginienses classem exussissent et exercitum dimisissent

summary_en: A theater contracted for by the censors was, on the motion of P. Cornelius Nasica, destroyed by decree of the senate as useless and harmful to public morals, and the people for some time watched the games standing.
quote_la: P. Cornelio Nasica auctore tamquam inutile et nociturum publicis moribus ex senatus consulto destructum est

summary_en: The Carthaginians made war on Masinissa contrary to the treaty, were defeated by him—then ninety-two years old—and in addition incurred war with Rome.
quote_la: Carthaginienses cum adversus foedus bellum Masinissae intulissent

summary_en: Disturbances in Syria and wars between its kings are related, in the course of which Demetrius, king of Syria, was killed.
quote_la: inter quos motus Demetrius Syriae rex occisus est.

summary_en: The Third Punic War began in the 602nd year from the founding of the city and was completed within the fifth year of its start.
quote_la: tertii Punici belli initium altero et sescentesimo ab urbe condita anno

summary_en: M. Porcius Cato and Scipio Nasica contended with opposing opinions, Cato urging war and that Carthage be removed and destroyed, Nasica arguing against it.
quote_la: Catone suadente bellum et ut tolleretur delereturque Carthago, Nasica dissuadente.

summary_en: It was resolved to declare war on the Carthaginians because they had ships contrary to the treaty, had led an army outside their borders, had borne arms against Rome's ally and friend Masinissa, and had refused to admit his son Gulussa into their city.
quote_la: placuit tamen, quod contra foedus naves haberent, quod exercitum extra fines duxissent

summary_en: Before any forces were embarked, envoys from Utica came to Rome surrendering themselves and all they had, an omen welcome to the senators and bitter to the Carthaginians.
quote_la: Uticenses legati Romam venerunt se suaque omnia dedentes.

summary_en: Games were held to Dis Pater at Tarentum in accordance with the Sibylline books, which had last been held a hundred years before, in the First Punic War, in the 502nd year of the city.
quote_la: ludi Diti patri ad Tarentum ex praecepto librorum facti

summary_en: Thirty envoys came to Rome through whom the Carthaginians surrendered themselves, but Cato's opinion prevailed that the decree stand and the consuls set out for war as soon as possible.
quote_la: legati triginta Romam venerunt, per quos se Carthaginienses dedebant.

summary_en: The consuls, after receiving 300 hostages and all arms and instruments of war at Carthage, ordered on the senate's authority that the Carthaginians build their town in another place no less than ten miles from the sea, driving them by this indignity to war.
quote_la: ut in alio loco, dum a mari decem milia passuum ne minus remoto, oppidum facerent

summary_en: Carthage began to be besieged and assaulted by the consuls L. Marcius and M'. Manilius.
quote_la: obsideri obpugnarique coepta est Carthago a L. Marcio M'. Manilio consulibus.

summary_en: In the assault Scipio extricated two tribunes who had rashly broken in with their cohorts, freed a Roman fort attacked by night with the help of a few horsemen, and won the chief glory for relieving the besieged camp.
quote_la: per quem et castellum Romanorum, quod nocte expugnabant, paucis equitibus iuvantibus liberatum est

summary_en: When the consul's army was routed by Hasdrubal in an unfavorable pass, as Scipio had warned, Scipio returned with a few squadrons of cavalry, freed the two besieged cohorts, and brought them back unharmed.
quote_la: cum paucis equitum turmis in saltum reversus liberavit eas et incolumes reduxit.

summary_en: Cato declared in the senate that the others serving in Africa flitted about as shadows while Scipio was full of vigor, and the Roman people so embraced him that most tribes voted him consul though his age did not permit it.
quote_la: reliquos, qui in Africa militarent, umbras volitare, Scipionem vigere

summary_en: When the tribune L. Scribonius proposed that the Lusitanians sold into slavery in Gaul by Ser. Galba be restored to freedom, Cato urged it fiercely, but Galba, pleading pitiably while embracing his young sons and his ward, secured the rejection of the bill.
quote_la: ita miserabiliter pro se locutus est, ut rogatio antiquaretur.

summary_en: Andriscus, a man of lowest station calling himself Philippus and son of king Perseus, escaped secretly from Rome, gathered an army with an invented tale of his royal birth, and occupied all Macedonia by consent or by arms.
quote_la: contracto exercitu totam Macedoniam aut voluntate incolentium aut armis occupavit.

summary_en: Thessaly, when Pseudophilippus wished to invade and occupy it, was defended through Roman envoys and Achaean auxiliaries.
quote_la: Thessalia, cum et illam invadere armis atque occupare Pseudophilippus vellet, per legatos Romanorum auxiliis Achaeorum defensa est.

summary_en: Prusias, king of Bithynia, a man of the basest vices, was killed by his son Nicomedes with the aid of Attalus, king of Pergamum.
quote_la: Prusias rex Bithyniae, omnium humillimorumque vitiorum, a Nicomede filio, adiuvante Attalo rege Pergami, occisus

summary_en: Of the three Roman envoys sent to make peace between Nicomedes and Prusias—one scarred on the head, one lame, one dull-witted—M. Cato said the embassy had neither head nor feet nor heart.
quote_la: M. Cato dixit eam in legationem, nec caput nec pedes nec cor habere.

summary_en: In Syria, while its slothful king lay in taverns and brothels, Hammonius ruled, through whom all the king's friends, queen Laodice, and Antigonus son of Demetrius were killed.
quote_la: Hammonius regnabat, per quem et amici omnes regis et Laodice regina et Antigonus Demetri filius occisi sunt.

summary_en: Masinissa, king of Numidia, died at more than ninety years, a distinguished man, so vigorous even in old age that he fathered a son after his eighty-sixth year.
quote_la: Masinissa Numidiae rex maior nonaginta annis decessit, vir insignis.

summary_en: P. Scipio Aemilianus, since Masinissa had left his kingdom jointly to his three sons Micipsa, Gulussa, and Mastanabal and bidden Scipio divide it, apportioned the administration of the kingdom among them.
quote_la: P. Scipio Aemilianus, cum commune his regnum pater reliquisset et dividere eos arbitro Scipione iussisset, partes administrandi regni divisit.

summary_en: Scipio persuaded Phameas Himilco, prefect of the Carthaginian cavalry, a brave man whose services the Carthaginians particularly used, to come over to the Romans with his cavalry.
quote_la: item Phameae Himilconi, praefecto equitum Carthaginiensium, viro forti et cuius praecipua opera Poeni utebantur, persuasit, ut ad Romanos cum equitatu suo transiret.

summary_en: Of the three envoys sent to Masinissa, M. Claudius Marcellus was overwhelmed by the waves in a storm that arose.
quote_la: M. Claudius Marcellus coorta tempestate fluctibus obrutus est.

summary_en: The Carthaginians killed in their senate-house Hasdrubal, grandson of Masinissa, whom they had as praetor, suspecting treason because he was a kinsman of Gulussa, who was aiding the Romans.
quote_la: Carthaginienses Hasdrubalem, Masinissae nepotem, quem praetorem habebant, hominem proditionis suspectum in curia occiderunt

summary_en: P. Scipio Aemilianus, while a candidate for the aedileship, was declared consul by the people and, since his age did not legally allow it, was exempted from the laws after a great struggle between the plebs and the resisting senators.
quote_la: P. Scipio Aemilianus cum aedilitatem peteret, consul a populo dictus.

summary_en: M'. Manilius stormed several cities situated around Carthage.
quote_la: M'. Manilius aliquot urbes circumpositas Carthagini expugnavit.

summary_en: Pseudophilippus in Macedonia, after cutting down the praetor P. Juventius with his army, was defeated and captured by Q. Caecilius, and Macedonia was recovered.
quote_la: Pseudophilippus in Macedonia, caeso cum exercitu P. Iuventio praetore, ab Q. Caecilio victus captusque est, et recepta Macedonia.

summary_en: Carthage, twenty-three miles in circuit, was besieged with great labor and captured piece by piece, first by the legate Mancinus, then by the consul Scipio, to whom Africa had been assigned outside the lot.
quote_la: magno labore obsessa et per partes capta est; primum a Mancino legato, deinde a Scipione consule

summary_en: The Carthaginians, after building a new harbor because the old one had been blocked by Scipio and secretly assembling a large fleet in a short time, fought a naval battle unsuccessfully.
quote_la: contracta clam exiguo tempore ampla classe infeliciter navali proelio pugnaverunt.

summary_en: The camp of their commander Hasdrubal, placed on difficult ground near the town of Nepheris, was destroyed with his army by Scipio.
quote_la: Hasdrubalis quoque, ducis eorum, castra ad Nepherim oppidum loco difficili sita cum exercitu deleta sunt a Scipione

summary_en: Scipio finally stormed Carthage in the seven hundredth year after its founding, and the greater part of the spoils was returned to the Sicilians from whom they had been taken.
quote_la: qui tandem expugnavit septingentesimo anno quam erat condita, spoliorum maior pars Siculis, quibus ablata erant, reddita.

summary_en: At the final destruction of the city, when Hasdrubal surrendered to Scipio, his wife, who days before had failed to persuade him to defect to the victor, threw herself with her two children from the citadel into the midst of the burning city.
quote_la: in medium se flagrantis urbis incendium cum duobus liberis ex arce praecipitavit.

summary_en: Scipio, following the example of his father Aemilius Paulus, conqueror of Macedonia, gave games and threw deserters and runaways to the beasts.
quote_la: Scipio exemplo patris sui Aemilii Pauli, qui Macedoniam vicerat, ludos fecit transfugasque ac fugitivos bestiis obiecit.

summary_en: The seeds of the Achaean war are related: Roman envoys, sent to detach from the Achaean league the cities that had been under Philip's rule, were assaulted by the Achaeans at Corinth.
quote_la: legati Romani ab Achaeis pulsati sint Corinthi, missi, ut eas civitates, quae sub dicione Philippi fuerant, ab Achaico concilio secernerent.

summary_en: Q. Caecilius Metellus fought at Thermopylae with the Achaeans, who had the Boeotians and Chalcidians as allies; on their defeat their leader Critolaus took his own life by poison.
quote_la: cum Achaeis, qui in auxilio Boeotos et Chalcidenses habebant, Q. Caecilius Metellus ad Thermopylas bello conflixit

summary_en: Diaeus, first instigator of the Achaean rising, chosen leader in Critolaus's place, was defeated at the Isthmus by consul L. Mummius.
quote_la: Diaeus, Achaici motus primus auctor, ab Achaeis dux creatus ad Isthmon a L. Mummio consule victus est.

summary_en: Mummius, having received all Achaea in surrender, destroyed Corinth by decree of the senate because the Roman envoys had been outraged there.
quote_la: omni Achaia in deditionem accepta Corinthon ex senatus consulto diruit, quia ibi legati Romani violati erant.

summary_en: Thebes and Chalcis, which had given aid, were also destroyed.
quote_la: Thebae quoque et Chalcis, quae auxilio fuerant, dirutae.

summary_en: L. Mummius conducted himself with the greatest integrity, and nothing from the works and ornaments of wealthy Corinth came into his house.
quote_la: nec quicquam ex his operibus ornamentisque, quae praedives Corinthos habuit, in domum eius pervenit.

summary_en: Q. Caecilius Metellus triumphed over Andriscus, and P. Cornelius Scipio Aemilianus over Carthage and Hasdrubal.
quote_la: Q. Caecilius Metellus de Andrisco triumphavit, P. Cornelius [Africanus] Scipio Aemilianus de Carthagine et Hasdrubale.

summary_en: Viriathus in Spain, first a shepherd turned hunter, then brigand, soon leader of a regular army, occupied all Lusitania, routed and captured the praetor M. Vetilius, and the praetor C. Plautius fared no better, so that a consular commander and army were needed against him.
quote_la: Viriathus in Hispania primum ex pastore venator, ex venatore latro, mox iusti quoque exercitus dux factus, totam Lusitaniam occupavit

summary_en: Demetrius son of Demetrius, scorning the sloth of Alexander who was ruling Syria, killed him in war with the help of Ptolemy, king of Egypt, whose daughter Cleopatra he had married.
quote_la: adiuvante Ptolemaeo Aegypti rege, cuius filiam Cleopatram in matrimonium acceperat, bello interemit.

summary_en: Ptolemy, gravely wounded in the head, died during treatment while the doctors were trying to trepan the bone, and his younger brother Ptolemy, who ruled at Cyrene, succeeded him.
quote_la: Ptolemaeus graviter in caput vulneratus inter curationem, dum ossa medici terebrare conantur, expiravit

summary_en: Demetrius, because of the cruelty he inflicted on his subjects through torture, was defeated in war by a certain Diodotus, who claimed the kingdom for Alexander's two-year-old son, and fled to Seleucia.
quote_la: ab Diodoto quodam, uno ex subiectis, qui Alexandri filio bimulo admodum regnum adserebat, bello superatus Seleuceam confugit.

summary_en: L. Mummius triumphed over the Achaeans, carrying bronze and marble statues and painted pictures in his triumph.
quote_la: L. Mummius de Achaeis triumphavit, signa aerea marmoreaque et tabulas pictas in triumpho tulit.

summary_en: Consul Appius Claudius subdued the Salassi, an Alpine people.
quote_la: Appius Claudius consul Salassos, gentem Alpinam, domuit.

summary_en: A second Pseudophilippus in Macedonia was cut down with his army by the quaestor L. Tremellius.
quote_la: alter Pseudophilippus in Macedonia a L. Tremellio quaestore cum exercitu caesus est.

summary_en: Q. Caecilius Metellus as proconsul slaughtered the Celtiberians.
quote_la: Q. Caecilius Metellus pro cos. Celtiberos cecidit

summary_en: A great part of Lusitania was recovered by the proconsul Q. Fabius after several cities were stormed.
quote_la: a Q. Fabio pro cos. pars magna Lusitaniae expugnatis aliquot urbibus recepta est.

summary_en: The senator Acilius wrote Roman history in Greek.
quote_la: Acilius senator Graece res Romanas scribit.

summary_en: Consul Q. Pompeius subdued the Termestini in Spain.
quote_la: Q. Pompeius consul in Hispania Termestinos subegit.

summary_en: With the Termestini and the Numantines Pompeius made a peace that was invalidated by the Roman people.
quote_la: cum isdem et Numantinis pacem a p. R. infirmatam fecit.

summary_en: The lustrum was closed by the censors: citizen heads counted were CCCXXVIII CCCCXLII (328,442).
quote_la: lustrum a censoribus conditum est: censa sunt civium capita CCCXXVIII CCCCXLII.

summary_en: When Macedonian envoys complained of the praetor D. Junius Silanus for despoiling the province after taking bribes, his father T. Manlius Torquatus obtained the inquiry for himself, condemned and disowned his son at home, and did not even attend the funeral when the son hanged himself.
quote_la: T. Manlius Torquatus, pater Silani, petit impetravitque, ut sibi cognitio mandaretur; et domi causa cognita filium condemnavit abdicavitque.

summary_en: The proconsul Q. Fabius, after successful operations in Spain, marred his record by making peace with Viriathus on equal terms.
quote_la: Q. Fabius pro cos. rebus in Hispania prospere gestis labem imposuit pace cum Viriatho aequis condicionibus facta.

summary_en: Viriathus was killed by traitors at the instigation of Servilius Caepio, greatly mourned by his army and nobly buried—a great man and leader, more often victorious in the fourteen years of his war with the Romans.
quote_la: Viriathus a proditoribus consilio Servilii Caepionis interfectus est et ab exercitu suo multum comploratus ac nobiliter sepultus

summary_en: While the consuls P. Cornelius Nasica Serapion and Dec. Junius Brutus held the levy, C. Matienius, accused before the tribunes of deserting the army in Spain, was condemned, long beaten with rods under the fork, and sold for a single sesterce.
quote_la: C. Matienius accusatus est apud tribunos plebis, quod exercitum ex Hispania deseruisset

summary_en: The tribunes of the plebs, failing to obtain the right each to exempt ten soldiers of their choosing, ordered the consuls led to prison.
quote_la: tribuni plebis quia non impetrarent, ut sibi denos, quos vellent, milites eximere liceret, consules in carcerem duci iusserunt.

summary_en: Consul Junius Brutus in Spain gave lands and a town called Valentia to those who had served under Viriathus.
quote_la: Iunius Brutus consul in Hispania iis, qui sub Viriatho militaverant, agros et oppidum dedit, quod vocatum est Valentia.

summary_en: M. Popilius was routed and put to flight with his army by the Numantines, with whom the senate had decreed the peace invalid.
quote_la: M. Popilius a Numantinis, cum quibus pacem factam irritam fieri senatus censuerat, cum exercitu fusus fugatusque est.

summary_en: When consul C. Hostilius Mancinus was sacrificing, the chickens flew from their coop, and as he boarded ship for Spain a voice was heard crying 'stay, Mancinus'—omens proved grim by the outcome.
quote_la: C. Hostilio Mancino consule sacrificante pulli ex cavea evolaverunt

summary_en: Mancinus, defeated by the Numantines and stripped of his camp, with no hope of saving the army, made an ignominious peace which the senate refused to ratify; XXXX (40,000) Romans had been defeated by four thousand Numantines.
quote_la: pacem cum his fecit ignominiosam, quam ratam esse senatus vetuit.

summary_en: Decimus Junius thoroughly subdued Lusitania as far as the Ocean by storming its cities, and when his men refused to cross the river Oblivion, he seized the standard from the bearer and carried it across himself, so persuading them to cross.
quote_la: Decimus Iunius Lusitaniam expugnationibus urbium usque ad Oceanum perdomuit

summary_en: The son of Alexander, king of Syria, a boy of barely ten, was treacherously killed by his guardian Diodotus, surnamed Tryphon, who bribed the doctors to kill him during surgery while telling the people he suffered from the stone.
quote_la: a Diodoto, qui Tryphon cognominabatur, tutore suo, per fraudem occisus est corruptis medicis

summary_en: Decimus Junius Brutus fought successfully against the Gallaeci in Further Spain.
quote_la: decimus Iunius Brutus in Hispania ulteriore feliciter adversus Gallaecos pugnavit.

summary_en: With unlike fortune the proconsul M. Aemilius Lepidus campaigned against the Vaccaei and suffered a disaster like that at Numantia.
quote_la: M. Aemilius Lepidus pro cos. adversus Vaccaeos rem gessit clademque similem Numantinae passus est.

summary_en: To release the people from the sanctity of the Numantine treaty, Mancinus, its author, was handed over to the Numantines, who did not receive him.
quote_la: Mancinus, cum huius rei auctor fuisset, deditus Numantinis non est receptus.

summary_en: The lustrum was closed by the censors: citizen heads counted were CCCXVII DCCCCXXXIII (317,933).
quote_la: lustrum a censoribus conditum est: censa sunt civium capita CCCXVII DCCCCXXXIII.

summary_en: Consul Fulvius Flaccus subdued the Vardaei in Illyricum.
quote_la: Fulvius Flaccus consul Vardaeos in Illyrico subegit.

summary_en: The praetor M. Cosconius fought successfully in Thrace with the Scordisci.
quote_la: M. Cosconius praetor in Thracia cum Scordiscis prospere pugnavit.

summary_en: Since the Numantine war dragged on through the fault of its commanders to public shame, the consulship was conferred unsought on Scipio Africanus by senate and people, and he was again exempted from the law forbidding a second consulship.
quote_la: delatus est ultro Scipioni Africano a senatu populoque Romano consulatus

summary_en: A slave war arose in Sicily, begun by the Syrian slave Eunus, who gathered a band of rural slaves, opened the slave-prisons, and made up the numbers of a regular army; when the praetors could not suppress it, it was entrusted to consul C. Fulvius.
quote_la: bellum servile in Sicilia ortum cum opprimi a praetoribus non potuisset, C. Fulvio consuli mandatum est.

summary_en: Cleon, a second slave, gathered as many as seventy thousand slaves, and with joined forces they repeatedly waged war against the Roman army.
quote_la: Cleon quoque alter servus ad septuaginta milia servorum contraxit; et iunctis copiis adversus exercitum Romanum bellum saepe gesserunt.

summary_en: Scipio Africanus besieged Numantia and recalled the army, corrupted by license and luxury, to the strictest military discipline, cutting away all instruments of pleasure and expelling two thousand prostitutes from the camp.
quote_la: Scipio Africanus Numantiam obsedit et corruptum licentia luxuriaque exercitum ad severissimam militiae disciplinam revocavit.

summary_en: Scipio kept the soldier daily at work, compelled him to carry thirty days' grain and seven stakes, and rebuked stragglers with sharp sayings.
quote_la: militem cotidie in opere habuit et triginta dierum frumentum ad septenos vallos ferre cogebat.

summary_en: Any soldier Scipio caught out of his rank he beat—with vine-rods if a Roman, with staves if a foreigner—and he sold all the pack animals so they should not relieve the soldiers of their loads.
quote_la: quem militem extra ordinem deprehendit, si Romanus esset, vitibus, si extraneus, virgis cecidit.

summary_en: Scipio often fought successfully against sorties of the enemy.
quote_la: saepe adversus eruptiones hostium feliciter pugnavit.

summary_en: The Vaccaei, under siege, slaughtered their children and wives and killed themselves.
quote_la: Vaccaei obsessi liberis coniugibusque trucidatis ipsi se interemerunt.

summary_en: Scipio declared he would accept the lavish gifts sent him by Antiochus, king of Syria, openly before the tribunal, ordered the quaestor to enter them in the public records, and said he would give gifts from them to brave men.
quote_la: Scipio amplissima munera missa sibi ab Antiocho rege Syriae

summary_en: Having enclosed Numantia on every side and seeing the besieged pressed by hunger, Scipio forbade killing enemies who went out to forage, saying that the more they were, the faster they would consume the grain they had.
quote_la: cum undique Numantiam obsidione clusisset et obsessos fame videret urgeri, hostes, qui pabulatum exierant, vetuit occidi

summary_en: The tribune Tib. Sempronius Gracchus, against the will of the senate and equestrian order, carried an agrarian law that no one should hold more than a thousand iugera of public land.
quote_la: cum legem agrariam ferret adversus voluntatem senatus et equestris ordinis, nequis ex publico agro plus quam mille iugera possideret

summary_en: In his frenzy Gracchus deposed by law his colleague M. Octavius, who defended the opposing side, and had himself, his brother C. Gracchus, and his father-in-law Appius Claudius created triumvirs for distributing the land.
quote_la: M. Octavio collegae causam diversae partis defendenti potestatem lege lata abrogaret

summary_en: Gracchus promulgated another agrarian law to open up more land for himself, that the same triumvirs should judge what was public and what private land.
quote_la: promulgavit et aliam legem agrariam, qua sibi latius agrum patefaceret, ut idem triumviri iudicarent, qua publicus ager, qua privatus esset.

summary_en: When there was less land than could be divided without offending the plebs, Gracchus announced he would propose a law that the money of king Attalus be distributed to those entitled to land under the Sempronian law.
quote_la: ut his, qui Sempronia lege agrum accipere deberent, pecunia, quae regis Attali fuisset, divideretur.

summary_en: Attalus, king of Pergamum, son of Eumenes, had left the Roman people his heir.
quote_la: heredem autem populum Romanum reliquerat Attalus, rex Pergami, Eumenis filius.

summary_en: The ex-consul T. Annius, after speaking against Gracchus in the senate, was dragged by him before the people and harangued against him again from the rostra.
quote_la: T. Annius consularis, qui cum in senatu in Gracchum perorasset, raptus ab eo ad populum

summary_en: When Gracchus sought re-election as tribune, he was killed on the Capitol by the optimates at the instigation of P. Cornelius Nasica, struck first with fragments of a bench, and was thrown unburied into the river among the others killed in the sedition.
quote_la: auctore P. Cornelio Nasica in Capitolio ab optimatibus occisus est, ictus primum fragmentis subsellii

summary_en: The book also contained operations against the runaway slaves in Sicily with varying outcome.
quote_la: res praeterea in Sicilia vario eventu adversus fugitivos gestas continet.

summary_en: The Numantines, driven by hunger, killed one another by turns; Scipio Africanus destroyed the captured city and triumphed over it in the fourteenth year after Carthage was destroyed.
quote_la: captam urbem Scipio Africanus delevit et de ea triumphavit, quarto decimo anno post Carthaginem deletam.

summary_en: Consul P. Rupilius finished the war with the runaway slaves in Sicily.
quote_la: P. Rupilius consul in Sicilia cum fugitivis debellavit.

summary_en: Aristonicus, son of king Eumenes, seized Asia, although by the testament of king Attalus it had been left to the Roman people and was to be free.
quote_la: Aristonicus Eumenis regis filius Asiam occupavit, cum testamento Attali regis legata populo Romano libera esse deberet.

summary_en: Consul P. Licinius Crassus, though also pontifex maximus—a thing never done before—set out beyond Italy against Aristonicus and was defeated in battle and killed.
quote_la: P. Licinius Crassus consul, cum idem pontifex maximus esset, quod numquam antea factum erat, extra Italiam profectus proelio victus et occisus est.

summary_en: Consul M. Perperna defeated Aristonicus and received his surrender.
quote_la: M. Perperna consul victum Aristonicum in deditionem accepit.

summary_en: Q. Pompeius and Q. Metellus, then for the first time both censors from the plebs, closed the lustrum: citizen heads counted were CCCXVIII DCCCXXIII (318,823), not counting orphan boys, orphan girls, and widows.
quote_la: censa sunt civium capita CCCXVIII DCCCXXIII, praeter pupillos pupillas et viduas.

summary_en: The censor Q. Metellus proposed that all men be compelled to take wives for the sake of producing children; his extant speech was read in the senate by Augustus Caesar, as if written for his own times, when dealing with the marriage of the orders.
quote_la: Q. Metellus censor censuit, ut cogerentur omnes ducere uxores liberorum creandorum causa.

summary_en: The tribune C. Atinius Labeo ordered the censor Q. Metellus, by whom he had been passed over in the revision of the senate, thrown from the rock, but the other tribunes came to the rescue.
quote_la: C. Atinius Labeo tribunus plebis Q. Metellum censorem, a quo senatu legendo praeteritus erat, de saxo deici iussit

summary_en: When the tribune Carbo proposed that it be lawful to elect the same man tribune as often as he wished, P. Africanus opposed it in a weighty speech, saying Ti. Gracchus seemed justly slain; C. Gracchus spoke for the proposal, but Scipio prevailed.
quote_la: rogationem eius P. Africanus gravissima oratione dissuasit; in qua dixit Ti. Gracchum iure caesum videri.

summary_en: Wars waged between Antiochus of Syria and Phraates, king of the Parthians, are related, and affairs in Egypt no more quiet.
quote_la: bella inter Antiochum Syriae et Prahaten Parthorum regem gesta nec magis quietae res Aegypti referuntur.

summary_en: Ptolemy surnamed Euergetes, hated by his people for his excessive cruelty, fled secretly to Cyprus when the mob burned his palace, and when the kingdom was given to his sister Cleopatra, he killed the son he had by her and sent the head, hands, and feet to the mother.
quote_la: infensus filium, quem ex illa habebat, in Cypro occidit caputque eius et manus et pedes matri misit.

summary_en: Seditions were stirred up by the triumvirs Fulvius Flaccus, C. Gracchus, and C. Papirius Carbo, created for dividing the land.
quote_la: seditiones a triumviris Fulvio Flacco et C. Graccho et C. Papirio Carbone agro dividendo creatis excitatae

summary_en: P. Scipio Africanus, who opposed the triumvirs, after returning home hale and strong the day before, was found dead in his bedroom; his wife Sempronia, sister of the Gracchi, was suspected of poisoning him, but no inquiry was held into his death.
quote_la: fortisque ac validus pridie domum se recepisset, mortuus in cubiculo inventus est.

summary_en: Consul C. Sempronius at first fared badly against the Iapydes, but soon redeemed the defeat with a victory won through the valor of Decimus Junius Brutus, the conqueror of Lusitania.
quote_la: C. Sempronius consul adversus Iapydas primo male rem gessit

summary_en: Consul L. Aurelius subdued the rebelling Sardinians.
quote_la: L. Aurelius consul rebellantes Sardos subegit.

summary_en: M. Fulvius Flaccus was the first to subdue the Transalpine Ligurians in war, sent to aid the Massiliotes against the Salluvian Gauls who were ravaging their territory.
quote_la: M. Fulvius Flaccus primus Transalpinos Liguras domuit bello, missus in auxilium Massiliensium adversus Salluvios Gallos

summary_en: The praetor L. Opimius received the surrender of the Fregellans, who had revolted, and destroyed Fregellae.
quote_la: L. Opimius praetor Fregellanos, qui defecerant, in deditionem accepit, Fregellas diruit.

summary_en: A pestilence in Africa is reported to have arisen from a huge multitude of locusts and then from the heaps of their dead bodies.
quote_la: pestilentia in Africa ab ingenti lucustarum multitudine et deinde necatarum strage fuisse traditur.

summary_en: The lustrum was closed by the censors: citizen heads counted were CCCXCIIII DCCXXXVI (394,736).
quote_la: lustrum a censoribus conditum est: censa sunt civium capita CCCXCIIII DCCXXXVI.

summary_en: The tribune C. Gracchus, more eloquent than his brother Tiberius, carried several pernicious laws: a grain law that grain be given to the plebs at six and a third asses, a second agrarian law like his brother's, and a third to corrupt the equestrian order by adding six hundred equites to the three hundred senators in the senate.
quote_la: perniciosas aliquot leges tulit, inter quas frumentariam, ut senis et triente frumentum plebi daretur

summary_en: His tribunate continued into a second year, C. Gracchus by agrarian laws brought about the founding of several colonies in Italy and one on the soil of destroyed Carthage, which he led out himself as triumvir.
quote_la: effecit, ut complures coloniae in Italia deducerentur, et una in solo dirutae Carthaginis

summary_en: The book also contained the campaign of consul Q. Metellus against the Baleares, whom the Greeks call Gymnesii because they pass the summer naked.
quote_la: praeterea res a Q. Metello consule adversus Baleares gestas continet

summary_en: Disturbances in Syria are also related, in which Cleopatra killed her husband Demetrius and her son Seleucus, angered that he had assumed the diadem without her leave after his father was killed by her.
quote_la: Cleopatra Demetrium virum suum et Seleucum filium, indignata, quod occiso patre eius a se iniussu suo diadema sumpsisset, interemit.
